I made this thing. It only took me about 140 hours and 5400 individually glued pieces.

It looks beautiful!
Could you elaborate on the material used and the building process especially keeping the aspect ration of the real thing.
Thank you for sharing.

Sure!
I found blue-prints for the Eiffel tower online. I printed them out on 11x17 paper, and used that as a template for dimensioning all the pieces.
It's a bit more complicated than that though, because turning it into a three dimensional model (by hand) required the building of fairly intricate paper/cardboard scaffolding to hold the pieces in place as the glue dried. Even when all was said and done, I had to tear out one of the middle sections columns, and completely rebuild it as the radius of the turn was all fucked up.

In the end, I think it came out really great. I've always had plans to paint it Eiffel grey and put in little LED lights inside, but, I've just never found myself with that amount of time (I made this back when I was unemployed during the recession for 2 years).

Well it sure looks great. I had a guess you used a 2D template for the dimensions. Turning that into a 3D standup structure using so many pieces must have been tricky. As you said, a few pieces off, and you had to redo a whole section. Great work though. It would sure look more impressive with a grey metal color finish.
